Let \(A\) be the origin, and set
\[
\mathbf b=\overrightarrow{AB},\qquad \mathbf c=\overrightarrow{AC}.
\]
Let
\[
S=|\mathbf b|^2+|\mathbf c|^2=11^2+13^2=290,\qquad p=\mathbf b\cdot \mathbf c.
\]

The centroid is
\[
\mathbf g=\frac{\mathbf b+\mathbf c}{3}.
\]
If \(\mathbf o=\overrightarrow{AO}\) is the circumcenter, then since \(OA=OB=OC\),
\[
\mathbf o\cdot \mathbf b=\frac{|\mathbf b|^2}{2},\qquad
\mathbf o\cdot \mathbf c=\frac{|\mathbf c|^2}{2}.
\]
Thus
\[
\mathbf g\cdot \mathbf o
=\frac{1}{3}(\mathbf b+\mathbf c)\cdot\mathbf o
=\frac{S}{6}.
\]

Let \(\mathbf h\) be the orthocenter of \(\triangle AGO\). The altitude from \(G\) is perpendicular to \(AO\), and the altitude from \(O\) is perpendicular to \(AG\), so
\[
\mathbf h\cdot\mathbf o=\mathbf g\cdot\mathbf o=\frac{S}{6},
\qquad
\mathbf h\cdot\mathbf g=\mathbf o\cdot\mathbf g=\frac{S}{6}.
\]

Since \(A\) is the origin and \(\mathbf b,\mathbf c\) form a basis of the plane, write
\[
\mathbf h=\alpha \mathbf b+\beta \mathbf c.
\]
From \(\mathbf h\cdot\mathbf o=S/6\),
\[
\alpha|\mathbf b|^2+\beta|\mathbf c|^2=\frac{S}{3}. \tag{1}
\]
From \(\mathbf h\cdot\mathbf g=S/6\),
\[
\alpha|\mathbf b|^2+\beta|\mathbf c|^2+p(\alpha+\beta)=\frac{S}{2}. \tag{2}
\]
Subtracting (1) from (2) gives
\[
p(\alpha+\beta)=\frac{S}{6}.
\]

Now \(H\) lies on line \(BC\). In the basis \((\mathbf b,\mathbf c)\), points on line \(BC\) have coordinate sum \(1\), so
\[
\alpha+\beta=1.
\]
Therefore
\[
p=\frac{S}{6}.
\]

Finally,
\[
BC^2=|\mathbf b-\mathbf c|^2
=|\mathbf b|^2+|\mathbf c|^2-2\mathbf b\cdot\mathbf c
=S-2p
=S-\frac{S}{3}
=\frac{2S}{3}.
\]
Thus
\[
BC^2=\frac{2\cdot 290}{3}=\frac{580}{3},
\]
so
\[
BC=\sqrt{\frac{580}{3}}=\frac{2\sqrt{435}}{3}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{2\sqrt{435}}{3}}
\]
